questions.question: Explain different molecular genetic techniques for Algal bioengineering.
questions.solution_html:
• Molecular genetic techniques are concerned with manipulating, reproducing, adding, and
  • deleting DNA and RNA molecules in an organism.
  • Manipulations, deletions, and additions are accomplished via genetic transformation and
  • genetic editing, while reproduction is accomplished via cloning.
  • Genetic transformation in algae involves introducing foreign DNA into nuclear or chloroplast
  • genomes using methods like electroporation, particle bombardment, Agrobacterium
  • mediated transfer, and glass bead agitation to alter metabolic pathways.
questions.final_answer: mediated transfer, and glass bead agitation to alter metabolic pathways

questions.question: Why is yeast prefered in the baking industry?
questions.solution_html:
• Yeast is preferred in the baking industry mainly because of how effectively it improves both
  • the texture and flavor of baked goods.
  • At its core, yeast works through a process called Fermentation. When added to dough, yeast
  • feeds on sugars and produces carbon dioxide gas and a small amount of alcohol. The gas gets
  • trapped in the dough, causing it to rise and become light and airy—this is what gives bread its
  • soft, fluffy structure.
questions.final_answer: soft, fluffy structure
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how fungi serve as model organisms in scientific research.
questions.solution_html:
• • Easy to culture: They grow quickly on simple, inexpensive media.
  • • Short life cycles: This allows rapid observation of multiple generations.
  • • Genetic simplicity: Many fungi have small, well-characterized genomes.
  • • Eukaryotic cells: Unlike bacteria, fungi have a nucleus and organelles, making them
  • more comparable to animal and plant cells.
  • • Genetic manipulation: They are easy to mutate and study genetically.
  • Common fungal model organisms
  • Saccharomyces cerevisiae; Schizosaccharomyces pombe; Neurospora crassa; Aspergillus
  • nidulans
questions.final_answer: nidulans

questions.question: Analyze the future prospects of algal biotechnology.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the future prospects of algal biotechnology.
  • Algal biotechnology is rapidly emerging as a critical component of the future green
  • bioeconomy, offering sustainable solutions for energy, nutrition, and environmental
  • management. As photosynthetic organisms, algae present a versatile "cell factory" for
  • producing high-value compounds, including biofuels, pharmaceuticals, pigments, and
  • nutritional supplements.
  • • Advanced Biofuels & Renewable Energy: Algae are considered the ultimate source for third
  • generation biofuels, including biodiesel, bioethanol, and biohydrogen. Future prospects lie in
  • increasing lipid productivity and optimizing thermochemical conversion technologies to make
  • algal fuels cost-competitive with fossil fuels.
  • • Pharmaceuticals and Nutraceuticals: Algae produce potent bioactive molecules, such as
  • carotenoids (astaxanthin, -carotene) and polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs), which have
  • antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties.
  • • Environmental Remediation (Phycoremediation): Algae are exceptionally effective at treating
  • industrial and municipal wastewater, removing nitrogen, phosphorus, and heavy metals while
  • producing usable biomass. They can also mitigate atmospheric emissions by capturing it
  • during photosynthesis, aiding in carbon footprint reduction.
  • • Bioproducts & Materials: algae are being used to develop sustainable alternatives to
  • petroleum-based products, including bioplastics, biodegradable fabrics, and high-value
  • pigments.
  • • Genetic Engineering & Synthetic Biology: The application of CRISPR-Cas9 and other genome
  • editing tools allows researchers to modify algal genomes for higher yields, resilience to harsh
  • conditions, and optimized nutrient synthesis
questions.final_answer: conditions, and optimized nutrient synthesis
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how fungi help in the breakdown of agro-residues.
questions.solution_html:
• Fungi play a crucial role in breaking down agro-residues (like. straw, husk, stalks, and leaves
  • left after harvest) by acting as nature’s primary recyclers. They decompose complex plant
  • materials and convert them into simpler substances that enrich the soil.
  • • Breaking down tough plant components
  • Agro-residues are rich in complex compounds such as: Cellulose,Hemicellulose, lignin
  • These are difficult for most organisms to digest. Fungi are. uniquely equipped to degrade
  • them using powerful enzymes
  • Cellulases break cellulose into simple sugars Hemicellulases break hemicelluloseLigninases
  • (like laccase and peroxidase) break down lignin, which is the hardest component
  • Turning residues into simpler organic matter As fungi grow on crop waste, they
  • • Absorb nutrients from the residues
  • Chemically break them into simpler organic compounds Convert them into humus-like
  • material
  • • Improving soil fertility
  • The breakdown process helps
  • Release nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium back into the soil Increase soil
  • organic matter
  • • Speeding up composting
  • Fungi are especially important in composting agricultural waste
  • They colonize residues early and soften tough plant fibers Work alongside bacteria and other
  • microbes
  • • Help faster and more efficient compost formation
  • Examples of useful fungi
  • Some fungi commonly involved include
  • White-rot fungi (efficient lignin degraders) Brown-rot fungi (mainly cellulose breakdown)
  • Species like Trichoderma and Pleurotus (oyster mushrooms), which are widely used in
  • agricultural waste decomposition
questions.final_answer: agricultural waste decomposition
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain how fungi help in the breakdown of agro-residues.
questions.solution_html:
• Fungi play a crucial role in breaking down agro-residues (like. straw, husk, stalks, and leaves
  • left after harvest) by acting as nature’s primary recyclers. They decompose complex plant
  • materials and convert them into simpler substances that enrich the soil.
  • • Breaking down tough plant components
  • Agro-residues are rich in complex compounds such as: Cellulose,Hemicellulose, lignin
  • These are difficult for most organisms to digest. Fungi are. uniquely equipped to degrade
  • them using powerful enzymes
  • Cellulases break cellulose into simple sugars Hemicellulases break hemicelluloseLigninases
  • (like laccase and peroxidase) break down lignin, which is the hardest component
  • Turning residues into simpler organic matter As fungi grow on crop waste, they
  • • Absorb nutrients from the residues
  • Chemically break them into simpler organic compounds Convert them into humus-like
  • material
  • • Improving soil fertility
  • The breakdown process helps
  • Release nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium back into the soil Increase soil
  • organic matter
  • • Speeding up composting
  • Fungi are especially important in composting agricultural waste
  • They colonize residues early and soften tough plant fibers Work alongside bacteria and other
  • microbes
  • • Help faster and more efficient compost formation
  • Examples of useful fungi
  • Some fungi commonly involved include
  • White-rot fungi (efficient lignin degraders) Brown-rot fungi (mainly cellulose breakdown)
  • Species like Trichoderma and Pleurotus (oyster mushrooms), which are widely used in
  • agricultural waste decomposition
questions.final_answer: agricultural waste decomposition
